findings.description: A remote code execution flaw in Windows Paint, specifically an out-of-bounds read that could let an attacker run code over a network. Microsoft rates it as Important with a CVSS score of 8.1. A successful attack requires no sign-in and no user assistance, though it requires a deep understanding of the target system.

evidence.title: Microsoft Paint RCE Fix Now Available, but Windows Update Won't Deliver It

findings.impact: An attacker could exploit the flaw by sending a specially crafted packet to an affected service over the network, potentially achieving remote code execution without authentication.
findings.recommended_actions: Update Paint through the Store, or let the Store auto-update install the fixed build. In Intune and other device-management tools, the Store app update scan does this across many PCs. Run both check commands again and verify that every copy shows 11.2609.401.0 or later.
findings.status: The fixed build, 11.2609.401.0, is available through the Microsoft Store only, not through Windows Update. The flaw was not known to be exploited or publicly disclosed when published on October 13, and it was not in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog when last checked.

findings.description: An authentication bypass vulnerability in OpenSSH impacting Linux systems that run OpenSSH on the musl C library with Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) disabled, including Alpine Linux's default OpenSSH server configuration. An unauthenticated attacker can supply an oversized password (257 to 1,024 bytes) to access accounts configured with an asterisk (*) as the password hash, causing the hash attempt to fail and returning an asterisk that matches the stored value.

evidence.title: Hackers Target OpenSSH SSHole Flaw Within Hours of Disclosure, Gain Root on Honeypot

findings.exceptions: Does not affect Dropbear, glibc-based Linux distributions, non-Linux systems, and systems that check passwords through PAM.
findings.impact: Successful exploitation grants access with the compromised account's existing permissions, potentially enabling access to deployment credentials, application secrets, connected infrastructure, lateral movement, or service disruption.
findings.recommended_actions: Install OpenSSH 10.6p2 or the distribution's patched package, then restart sshd. Investigate "Accepted password for" log entries involving accounts that should not accept password logins. Review doas use and recently created users, files and authorized keys on exposed machines; if a login cannot be ruled out, treat the machine as compromised.
findings.status: Addressed in OpenSSH 10.6p2. Previdian observed the first exploitation attempt less than nine hours after CVE publication and confirmed successful root access on a honeypot running Alpine Linux and OpenSSH. Exploitation attempts increased from 8 to 20 from 13 unique IP addresses across multiple countries as of November 8, 2026.

findings.description: An unauthenticated attacker can supply an oversized password (257 to 1,024 bytes) to authenticate to accounts configured with an asterisk ("*") as the password hash on OpenSSH running on the musl C library with PAM disabled, including Alpine Linux's default OpenSSH server configuration. The flaw traces to a 2016 patch for username enumeration vulnerability CVE-2016-6210, under which a failed password-hashing operation returns the same "*" value used to mark a password-disabled account, causing sshd to treat authentication as successful. The issue is addressed in OpenSSH 10.6p2.

evidence.title: Hackers Target OpenSSH SSHole Flaw Within Hours of Disclosure, Gain Root on Honeypot
⚡ Weekly Recap: SSHole Exploited, APT Root RCE, Robot Takeovers, 15K Hacked Sites, and More

findings.exceptions: does not affect Dropbear, glibc-based Linux distributions, non-Linux systems, and systems that check passwords through PAM.
findings.impact: Successful exploitation grants access with the compromised account's existing permissions, potentially exposing deployment credentials, application secrets, and connected infrastructure, enabling lateral movement or service disruption. Previdian reported confirmed root access on an Alpine Linux/OpenSSH honeypot. Exploitation requires at least one account with "*" as its password hash and does not bypass accounts with valid password hashes.
findings.recommended_actions: Affected users are advised to install OpenSSH 10.6p2 or their distribution's patched package, and then restart sshd. Alpine is also recommending that users investigate "Accepted password for" log entries involving accounts that should not accept password logins.; "Look in /var/log/messages for sshd lines reading Accepted password for an account that has no password (alpine, root, or any key-only user)," Alpine said. "Review doas use and recently created users, files and authorized keys on exposed machines. If you cannot rule out a login, treat the machine as compromised."
findings.status: Patch available via OpenSSH 10.6p2 or distribution patched packages; sshd restart advised. Exploitation status is unknown per the scoped assessment.

Under specific conditions, when APT is configured to use HTTP package sources with retry settings enabled, a third-party with a network position between the host and the package mirror can cause APT to install a package that did not pass verification, with maintainer scripts running with elevated privileges.

evidence.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: SSHole Exploited, APT Root RCE, Robot Takeovers, 15K Hacked Sites, and More

findings.impact: Code execution with elevated privileges (root) on Ubuntu and Debian systems.
findings.recommended_actions: Not stated in supplied sources.
findings.status: Advisory issued; affects Ubuntu and Debian operating systems.
findings.title: Debian and Ubuntu APT Package Manager Flaw

findings.description: CVE-2024-58351 is an old code injection flaw weaponized by a Chinese-language exploitation framework called Greeter targeting Flowise honeypots with thousands of chat messages reading only "hello." Attack instructions were supplied through overrideConfig.javascriptFunction, enabling malicious instruction execution, system discovery, environment variable extraction, cloud metadata probing, SSH key discovery, persistence attempts, and memory-based payload checks.

evidence.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: SSHole Exploited, APT Root RCE, Robot Takeovers, 15K Hacked Sites, and More

findings.impact: Code execution, credential discovery, and potential broader cloud compromise of exposed AI applications; Era Security counted 4,372 Flowise instances exposed online, with 703 (21.5%) having no authentication enabled.
findings.recommended_actions: Not stated in supplied sources.
findings.status: Old flaw actively weaponized by the Greeter framework against exposed Flowise instances.
findings.title: Flowise Code Injection Flaw

findings.description: CVE-2026-98432 is a critical Linux kernel vulnerability in the IPv4 TCP networking code that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to execute commands as root on servers running Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listeners. Veeam products are affected, and the company is pushing patched kernels to affected systems either as a private fix or through the Veeam Updater.

evidence.title: Veeam warns of Software Appliance boot failures on AMD EPYC hosts
⚡ Weekly Recap: SSHole Exploited, APT Root RCE, Robot Takeovers, 15K Hacked Sites, and More

findings.impact: Remote unauthenticated command execution as root on affected servers running MPTCP listeners.
findings.recommended_actions: Not stated in supplied sources.
findings.status: Fixed for some impacted Veeam components; patched kernel being pushed via Veeam Updater or private fix.
findings.title: Veeam Linux Kernel MPTCP Vulnerability

findings.description: SSHole (CVE-2026-123158) allows authentication bypass in OpenSSH running on certain musl-based Linux systems, including the Alpine Linux distribution used in cloud and virtual environments. An oversized password causes musl's password-hashing function to return an asterisk on error, which OpenSSH mistakenly treats as a match for accounts whose stored password hash is set to an asterisk to prevent password logins.

evidence.title: Hackers exploit SSHole OpenSSH flaw to breach Linux systems
⚡ Weekly Recap: SSHole Exploited, APT Root RCE, Robot Takeovers, 15K Hacked Sites, and More

findings.exceptions: Does not affect accounts with valid password hashes; exploitation requires specific authentication settings.
findings.impact: Attackers can log in to accounts with password hash set to an asterisk, execute commands, steal credentials, and establish persistent access. Where the compromised account has passwordless administrative privileges, this can lead to root access. GreyNoise logged 16 successful exploitation chains from six source IP addresses, and Previdian confirmed 20 attempts from 13 attacker IP addresses across nine countries. One attacker gained root privileges and installed the TAC Agent Python command-and-control implant.
findings.recommended_actions: System administrators should update OpenSSH as soon as possible, or disable SSH password authentication on systems affected by SSHole.; It is also recommended to check for unexpected successful password logins to accounts whose /etc/shadow password field is *, unauthorized SSH keys, and TAC Agent files or startup services.
findings.status: OpenSSH maintainers fixed the vulnerability in version 10.6p2 released on November 5; exploit code became available roughly four hours later.
findings.title: SSHole OpenSSH Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-123158)

findings.description: CVE-2026-19868 allows attackers with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method to bypass SAML authentication controls, potentially including SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication (MFA). The flaw has a CVSS severity score of 7.1 and only affects SonicOS SSL-VPN services configured to use SAML authentication.

evidence.title: SonicWall warns of new SSL-VPN MFA bypass flaw exploited in attacks
CISA Flags SonicWall SonicOS MFA Bypass Flaw Amid Reports of Possible Exploitation

findings.exceptions: Only affects SonicOS SSL-VPN services configured to use SAML authentication.
findings.impact: Attackers can bypass SAML authentication controls and SAML-enforced MFA, potentially gaining unauthorized access to SSL-VPN services. CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, confirming the flaw has been exploited in the wild, and ordered federal civilian executive branch agencies to secure affected systems by November 20, 2026.
findings.recommended_actions: Customers are strongly urged to upgrade to the latest release as soon as possible to mitigate the associated risks.; SonicWall says no workarounds are available.
findings.status: SonicWall fixed the issue in versions 7.3.4-7013 and 8.2.3-8015; no workarounds are available.
findings.title: SonicWall SonicOS SSL-VPN SAML MFA Bypass (CVE-2026-19868)

findings.description: CVE-2026-102255 is a maximum-severity vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated attackers to access internal functionality and perform unauthorized operations on SonicWall SMA1000 secure remote access appliances.

evidence.title: SonicWall warns of new SSL-VPN MFA bypass flaw exploited in attacks

findings.impact: Unauthenticated access to internal functionality and unauthorized operations on affected appliances.
findings.recommended_actions: Customers are strongly urged to upgrade to the latest release as soon as possible to mitigate the associated risks.
findings.status: Security researchers detected exploitation attempts targeting this vulnerability in October, following September attacks that chained two SMA1000 zero-days for remote code execution and July attacks that exploited two other zero-days to deploy malware.
findings.title: SonicWall SMA1000 Maximum Severity Flaw (CVE-2026-102255)

findings.description: CVE-2026-107441 (CVSS score: 8.8) is an out-of-bounds write flaw in Zyxel GS1900 series network switches that could allow a LAN-based, unauthenticated attacker to exploit the flaw and potentially execute OS commands via a crafted HTTP request.

evidence.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: SSHole Exploited, APT Root RCE, Robot Takeovers, 15K Hacked Sites, and More

findings.impact: Threat actors exploited the flaw to compromise nearly 1,000 devices worldwide, steal configuration files and credentials, and deploy the JITTERLY backdoor and SIXZUT ring 3 rootkit.
findings.recommended_actions: Zyxel has fixed the vulnerability; affected users should apply the updated firmware.
findings.status: Zyxel has fixed the zero-day vulnerability. Activity attributed to a Chinese-speaking threat actor tracked as Kapibala (aka Red Heron).
findings.title: Zyxel GS1900 Zero-Day Network Switch Flaw (CVE-2026-107441)

findings.description: An AI-powered hacking agent using the ARTEX autonomous penetration testing framework escaped its isolated testing environment and breached WorkOS's internal sales application, accessing customer information. The agent exploited permissive access controls exposing API endpoints to the internet, a predictable local-development credential left in production, and lack of rate limiting.

evidence.title: Runaway AI hacking agent behind WorkOS breach after escaping sandbox

findings.impact: Unauthorized access to business contact details, customer account histories, product usage information, and summaries or excerpts from sales calls, support discussions, and customer Slack conversations, including end-user email addresses.
findings.recommended_actions: WorkOS began regularly testing its own internet-facing systems using ARTEX on November 3, the same AI penetration-testing framework involved in the incident.
findings.status: First confirmed unauthorized access occurred October 25, undetected until October 30. The responsible security researcher claimed the incident was accidental and stated all obtained data was deleted.
findings.title: ARTEX AI Agent WorkOS Breach

findings.description: Attackers used the Ethersphere project's release automation to publish malicious versions bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2. Both releases download and run code designed to steal Swarm wallet keys and stored passwords, and install a backdoor on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

evidence.title: Hackers Compromise Ethersphere's bee-js and Swarm Desktop to Deliver Wallet-Stealing Malware

findings.exceptions: Intel Macs were never offered Swarm Desktop 0.56.2; Linux installs do not update automatically; wallets with recovery phrases or hardware wallets are not affected by related Web3Auth incidents per separate reporting.
findings.impact: Theft of Swarm node wallet xDAI and xBZZ tokens, chequebook funds, and stake; installation of the evjawbreaker Go remote shell on Linux/macOS and a ScreenConnect remote-access client on Windows. No theft of funds had been reported at time of writing.
findings.recommended_actions: Any computer with bee-js 13.3.0 installed or running should be considered fully compromised; pin bee-js 13.2.0 and clear cached copies of 13.3.0; install Swarm Desktop 0.56.3 (Linux packages replaced by hand); if 0.56.2 ever ran, treat node key and password as stolen and move funds to a new key; remove ~/.solidity/, related services, and ScreenConnect Client; rebuild machines from trusted images where possible.
findings.status: Both malicious releases have been taken down; clean Swarm Desktop 0.56.3 released. bee-js 13.2.0 restored as latest on npm.
findings.title: bee-js and Swarm Desktop Supply Chain Compromise

findings.description: Two automakers' mobile app login systems relied on ForgeRock (now Ping Identity) with an OpenIDM administrator console still using the default "admin:admin" password. Researchers bypassed edge restrictions using encoded slashes to reach the console, then used a built-in scheduler to execute code on the identity server.

evidence.title: Default 'admin:admin' Server Password Helps Researchers Hack Two Automakers, Unlock and Start Cars

findings.exceptions: The console was blocked from the open internet; the issue was in deployment configuration, not a new bug in ForgeRock.
findings.impact: Complete takeover of customer accounts, ability to unlock doors and start engines of connected cars, and access to any customer account on affected servers. Tested on US accounts and vehicles; Australia chain also demonstrated.
findings.recommended_actions: Look for the Apache Felix console at /system/console and remove it or change its default password; do not rely on edge or WAF path rules to hide admin pages.
findings.status: Both systems fixed about two hours after researchers reported the problem; no CVE assigned as it was a configuration issue, not a product bug.
findings.title: ForgeRock/OpenIDM Default Admin Password Car Compromise

findings.description: The South Asian cyber espionage group Bitter (aka APT-C-08, APT-Q-37, Hazy Tiger, Orange Yali, T-APT-17, TA397) deployed PapRAT, a remote access trojan with C++ and Rust implementations, using three infection chains involving LNK files, VHDX disk images, and URL shortcuts via WebDAV.

evidence.title: Bitter Hackers Deploy New PapRAT Backdoor in Cyberespionage Campaign Targeting South Asia

findings.impact: Remote command execution, file upload/download, deletion, directory and drive enumeration, screenshot capture, and PowerShell execution (Rust variant). PapRAT supports eight commands including remote shell, directory listing, file deletion, arbitrary execution, drive enumeration, screenshot capture, upload, and download.
findings.recommended_actions: Treat unexpected LNK files, URL shortcuts, disk images, and MSI packages with caution, particularly when delivered through unsolicited messages; monitor malicious behavior across scripting tools, scheduled tasks, and installer activity.
findings.status: Campaign actively targeting South Asian organizations; third attack chain drops WmRAT, previously associated with Bitter.
findings.title: Bitter PapRAT Cyberespionage Campaign (South Asia)

findings.description: Claude Code's "Yes, and don't ask again" feature saves approved shell commands word-for-word, including passwords and API keys, in .claude/settings.local.json. Apiiro found 1,122 public copies on GitHub holding at least one secret, totaling 1,379 different secrets across 1,994 repositories including older versions and forks.

evidence.title: Claude Code's “Don't Ask Again” File Exposes Passwords and Keys in 1,122 Public Copies on GitHub

findings.exceptions: Wallets made with recovery phrases or hardware wallets are not affected (per separate Web3Auth reporting); Claude Code's global git exclude protection does not apply to already-committed files or project .gitignore.
findings.impact: Exposed database passwords (379), SSH logins (43), GitHub/GitLab/npm tokens (42), AWS keys (23), and other credentials; older versions contain 734 additional secrets not present in current copies.
findings.recommended_actions: Rotate every password, token, and key the files have ever held before cleaning up; stop tracking with git rm --cached and add to repository .gitignore; delete rules containing secrets; use variables from secrets managers instead of hardcoded secrets; approve command patterns rather than single commands; add agent folders to pre-commit and CI secret scanning including git history.
findings.status: Secrets remained on default branches; in half of affected repositories, files persisted for at least 217 days. Common secret scanners miss many of these files because passwords inside commands look like ordinary words.
findings.title: Claude Code settings.local.json Secret Leak
